title: Taking the tutorial before a real run
target: What the tutorial level in R.E.P.O. actually is, given that the game ships a level of its own for it, runs it with a director, builds it from its own floors, walls and doors, and ends it at the truck.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A fresh copy of the game
A crew that has not played it before

steps.do: Start it from the menu rather than from a real level.
steps.because: a button in the menu leads into the tutorial, and the game ships a tutorial level of its own (Menu Button - Tutorial, Start Room - Tutorial)

steps.do: Expect a director to guide you through it.
steps.because: the tutorial is run by a director of its own (Tutorial Director)

steps.do: Treat its rooms as the tutorial's own rather than as a sample of a real level.
steps.because: the tutorial is built from its own floors, walls and doors (Tutorial Floor, Tutorial Wall, Tutorial Door)

steps.do: Look at the damaged part rather than going around it.
steps.because: part of it is deliberately damaged and ships a broken wall, with its own text container (Tutorial Broken Wall, Tutorial Text Container)

steps.do: Finish at the truck, through the trigger the tutorial uses.
steps.because: the tutorial ends at the truck through a trigger of its own (TutorialTruckTrigger, Truck Tutorial, Tutorial Truck Trigger)

commonMistakes: Skipping it and learning the controls in the middle of a real run.
Assuming the tutorial's rooms behave like a generated level.
Leaving before the truck trigger and missing the end of the lesson.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
